text:
Maria: Perf alert during nightly e2e on 8x-A100 — PP bubble latency spike, overall tail +38%.
Ajay: on it. which run/id?
Maria: run=2026-03-17-23:40 id=run-9182. uploading traces -> http://perf.internal/runs/9182/flame.svg
Linh: quick summary from the trace: forward all-reduce wall time jumped ~2.7x, and KV-cache hit rate fell ~12% vs baseline.
Carter: hm. any kernel selector changes merged yesterday? I remember a change touching fused-attn heuristics.
Zhao: I grabbed nvprof + NCCL timeline for the run. paste of key numbers below:
```
Forward allreduce avg: 32.1ms -> 84.7ms
Backward allreduce avg: 28.3ms -> 61.9ms
KV-cache hit: 88% -> 76%
Scheduler wake latency (1F1B): median 1.4ms -> 3.8ms
```
Nina: that increase in small allreduces smells like reduced coalescing — maybe kernel selector switched to a less-coalescable layout.
Ajay: I linked the PR: commit abc1234 changed attention kernel selection to prefer the stable fwd kernel when seq_len>1024 to avoid numerical drift.
Maria: that commit rolled into canary yesterday at 22:10, aligns with the time window.
Carter: suggestion: test a canary toggle to force old kernel selection and also bump microbatch from 4->8 to increase allreduce payload size (coalesce).
Linh: we should also inspect KV-cache eviction churn — if hit rate drops, more KV traffic increases small comm ops.
Zhao: ran a quick sim: forcing microbatch=8 reduces number of allreduces by ~2x and increases mean allreduce payload from 64KB->128KB.
Ajay: I'll run two quick experiments: (1) rollback kernel selector to prior behavior, (2) enable coalesced_allreduce=true + microbatch=8 in a canary pool.
Maria: schedule both sequentially to isolate effects. start with coalescing toggle since it's lower-risk.
ci-bot: deploy request queued: canary/pp-pool (2 nodes) — request id canary-3321
perf-bot: automated job started -> collecting traces for canary-3321. ETA 30m
Nina: also add a nightly KV-cache metric check to detect regressions early — alert if hit_rate drops >5%.
Carter: if coalescing fixes latency but hurts memory, we may need a hybrid: coalesce only for small-message bursts (detected by runtime). consider adaptive threshold.
Linh: note for 1F1B tuning: increasing microbatch reduces bubble frequency but increases per-stage compute; keep an eye on peak memory and per-GPU load balance.
Zhao: logging note: add a compact CSV row for allreduce counts/bytes per step in the trace so we can easily diff runs.
Maria: agreed. Action items: Ajay run canary with coalesced_allreduce + microbatch=8 (A), then kernel rollback test (B). Nina add KV-cache alert. Zhao add CSV logging. Carter explore adaptive coalescer design.
Ajay: starting A now, will post results in ~40m. tagging @everyone who worked on pp bubble heuristics :rocket:
Maria: thanks. keep thread for quick updates, we'll escalate to an oncall postmortem if A doesn't help.
perf-bot: canary-3321 job finished: preliminary numbers -> tail latency -22% vs spike run, KV-cache hit stable. Full traces at http://perf.internal/runs/canary-3321
Ajay: preliminary looks promising for coalescing. will run B next.
Maria: sweet. please paste final nvprof numbers when B completes. :thumbsup:
